text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTWN(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
HoldCitizenship(x, y) ::: x holds citizenship y.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Gazprom ::: Gazprom.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote can participate in the election.
CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegister(x) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register.
CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTWN(x) ::: Everyone has either US or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(Vladimir, Taiwanese) ::: Vladimir does not hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Vladimir is not a manager at Gazprom.
¬HoldCitizenship(Vladimir, Taiwanese) ∧ ¬Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ Manager(Ekaterina, Gazprom) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote, or she is a manager at Gazprom.
Conclusion:
CanParticipate(Ekaterina) ∨ Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the election, or Vladimir is a manager at Gazprom.
